details.title: Dependency Confusion: How I Hacked Into Apple, Microsoft and Dozens of Other Companies
details.summary: Publishing a package to a public registry under the name of a company's private internal dependency. Build tooling that consults both an internal index and the public one picks the highest version number, so the attacker's package is installed and its install script runs code inside the corporate network. It worked against more than 35 organisations.

2021-1.label: HTTP/2: The Sequel is Always Worse

details.title: HTTP/2: The Sequel is Always Worse
details.summary: HTTP/2 front-ends that downgrade requests to HTTP/1.1 lose the binary length field, so the back-end must trust an attacker-supplied Content-Length or Transfer-Encoding. This gives H2.CL and H2.TE desyncs, plus header and request-line injection through newlines and colons. An attacker can hijack other users' requests, poison caches and steal credentials.

Dynamic client registration accepts attacker URLs in logo_uri, jwks_uri and request_uris, giving second-order SSRF; keeping redirect_uri in the session lets a second request poison it and steal the code; and the WebFinger endpoint allows user enumeration and LDAP injection.

2021-8.label: HTTP Smuggling via Higher HTTP Versions

details.title: HTTP Request Smuggling via higher HTTP versions
details.summary: Request smuggling against front ends that terminate HTTP/2 or HTTP/3 and forward HTTP/1.1. Because HTTP/2 header names and values are binary strings that may contain newlines and colons, and content-length and transfer-encoding are not revalidated on downgrade, an attacker can inject a second request into the backend stream. Includes detection methods and a tool.

2021-9.label: Fuzzing for XSS via nested parsers condition

details.title: Fuzzing for XSS via nested parsers condition
details.summary: When two markup parsers run in sequence over the same message, the first parser output becomes the second parser input, letting injected markup escape an attribute value into attribute-name position. Fuzz lists that plant convertible markup inside other markup found this cross-site scripting in vBulletin, MyBB, PMWiki, Rocket.Chat, XMB, SMF and PunBB.

details.title: Universal Deserialisation Gadget for Ruby 2.x-3.x
details.summary: A gadget chain built only from Ruby's default classes turns an untrusted Marshal.load into arbitrary command execution, running from Gem::Requirement through Gem::Package::TarReader and Net::BufferedIO to Net::WriteAdapter, which calls any chosen method on any object. It replaces the earlier gadget patched in Ruby 2.7 and works from Ruby 2.0 to 3.0 with no extra gems loaded.

2021-11.label: The Secret Parameter, LFR, and Potential RCE in NodeJS Apps

details.title: The Secret Parameter, LFR, and Potential RCE in NodeJS Apps
details.summary: Express passes the whole render options object to the hbs view engine, which reads its layout property as a template path. A request body carrying a layout key therefore makes the server read and render an arbitrary file, giving local file read and, on old Handlebars versions, remote code execution. Prototype pollution can inject layout even when the app wraps its object.

details.summary: Homebrew's cask repository auto-approved pull requests using the git_diff Ruby gem, whose parser treats an added line matching a b/path pattern as file metadata rather than a content change. 2021-29.label: LEXSS: Bypassing Lexical Parsing Security Controls

details.title: LEXSS: Bypassing Lexical Parsing Security Controls
details.summary: HTML sanitisers that re-parse markup can be desynchronised from the browser's own parser. Nesting tags that switch tokenizer state, such as an iframe wrapping a textarea, or entering the MathML namespace, makes the sanitiser treat active content as harmless text, so the final parse executes it. Shown against TinyMCE and Froala.

2021-31.label: A Scientific Notation Bug in MySQL exposed AWS WAF

details.title: 24/7 managed detection, response, and expert cybersecurity services
details.summary: MySQL and MariaDB silently discard a malformed scientific-notation token such as 1.e when no digit follows the e, so the query stays valid while looking like nonsense to anything else parsing it. Injecting that token made SQL injection payloads unrecognisable to AWS WAF and to ModSecurity with libinjection, restoring injection against protected sites.

SAML libraries read the identity before validating the signature but validate after a round-trip, so one signed document logs an attacker in as anyone.

details.title: Talking About My Generation: Targeted DOM-based XSS Exploit Generation using Dynamic Data Flow Analysis
details.summary: Generates DOM XSS exploits using dynamic taint traces to identify replaceable URL ranges, preserve surrounding URL structure, and choose context-breaking payloads. The evaluation confirms 7,199 flows across 711 domains using a browser configured for legacy URL-encoding behavior.

2021-54.label: Towards a Lightweight, Hybrid Approach for Detecting DOM XSS Vulnerabilities with Machine Learning

details.title: Towards a Lightweight, Hybrid Approach for Detecting DOM XSS Vulnerabilities with Machine Learning
details.summary: Trains a neural classifier on JavaScript function tokens to select code for DOM XSS taint tracking. Its hybrid design retains 94.5% of unique confirmed vulnerabilities while modeling a 3.43-fold reduction in taint-tracking cost; the classifier alone has inadequate precision.

2021-55.label: Improper Spring @Query Usage Allows N1QL Injection

details.title: Improper Spring @Query Usage Allows N1QL Injection
details.summary: Compares Spring Data Couchbase queries that bind parameters with annotations that interpolate untrusted input through SpEL. A diagnostic quote reveals the generated N1QL statement, and a Spring test application plus a request-body repair for N1QLMap demonstrates the difference between safe binding and injectable query construction.

details.context: Author explicitly investigates the behavior raised in this earlier declined report.

details.title: Finding 0day to hack Apple
details.summary: Examines a Lucee administration flaw where privileged side effects occur before authentication is enforced. The Apple case study combines a restricted file write with search-index processing and describes an alternative virtual-filesystem route.

2021-57.label: XSinator.com: From a Formal Model to the Automatic Evaluation of Cross-Site Leaks in Web Browsers

details.title: XSinator.com: From a Formal Model to the Automatic Evaluation of Cross-Site Leaks in Web Browsers
details.summary: Separates response differences, inclusion methods and observable channels into a model for testing browser cross-site leaks. Controlled server states and browser adapters support repeatable comparisons, with additional global-limit and performance channels. The suite evaluates browser behavior; it does not automatically discover vulnerable website states. Extraction note: consult the original PDF for the attackable/safe circle symbols in Tables 2–4; their extracted glyph shapes differ.

details.context: The paper describes the accompanying browser evaluation suite hosted at this project site.
